Charles Sanders Peirce

Quotes / Charles Sanders Peirce / Q0486

English

Consider what effects… we conceive the object of our conception to have. Then, our conception of these effects is the whole of our conception of the object.
Thinker Charles Sanders Peirce
School Pragmatism
Source How to Make Our Ideas Clear
Theme Philosophy
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with How to Make Our Ideas Clear, within the tradition of Pragmatism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of philosophy, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Charles Sanders Peirce's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
